newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Outlaw gangs step up attacks in Albania.
newsitem.headline: Outlaw gangs step up attacks in Albania.

text.p: Heavily-armed outlaw gangs have staged attacks from the Albanian capital to the southern border with Greece in the past 48 hours despite the impending deployment of an Italian-led multinational security force.
Gunmen fired at the U.S. ambassador's residence in Tirana on Thursday, hitting cars, and an outlaw gang forced its way into the Greek consulate near the border to demand visas.
Lawlessness which has swept the Balkan country for three months has shown no sign of abating despite the plans to deploy a 6,000-strong Italian-led multinational security force.
No one was wounded in the shooting at the U.S. residential compound, where Ambassador Marisa Lino lives. Bullets hit three cars, police said.
Police raided homes near the U.S. residential compound, seizing a quantity of weapons and arresting several people.
Most foreign diplomats were flown out of Albania last month as the country plunged into anarchy following the collapse of a string of popular, but fraudulent, investment schemes.
Prime Minister Bashkim Fino returned from a visit to Athens and secured much-needed support from the European Union and the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE).
EU, OSCE and Greek officials assured Fino, 34, that his all-party crisis government would get organisational, economic and humanitarian aid as well as an Italian-led force to protect relief supplies.

"My visit was successful. The government of Prime Minister Costas Simitis will give us urgent economic aid, including food and medicine," Fino said on his return to Tirana. "In the next two days we shall receive substantial material assistance for the police from Greece."

Albania's military and police turned tail and ran in March when faced with a widespread popular uprising against President Sali Berisha, blamed for the failed savings schemes. Much of Albania, especially in the south, is no longer under government control.
Berisha was forced on March 11 to appoint Fino, an opposition Socialist, prime minister. Berisha also agreed to early general elections in June.

Fino met Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi before going to Greece. In Athens he met Simitis, special OSCE envoy Franz Vranitzky and Dutch Foreign Minister Hans van Mierlo, whose country holds the rotating EU presidency.
Several EU states, notably Greece, Italy and France, have been the driving force behind the multinational force which is due to be deployed in the next two weeks.

The force, which is being sent to protect humanitarian aid operations, is seen as crucial to stabilising the country and ensuring that the June election takes place. It is also aimed at heading off any mass movement of illegal immigrants.

The OSCE will play a crucial role in monitoring the June election and preventing irregularities, which the OSCE said took place when Berisha's right-wing Democratic Party won national elections last May.
